competences: The learner identifies key facts about types of district leaders.
The learner explains the roles of district leaders using the sourced local-government materials.
languageCompetence: Learners read, write and pronounce: leader, councillor, district, local government, speaker, civic and political.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to use sourced questions to distinguish political, civic and other leaders.
By the end of the lesson learners should be able to answer original source questions about district leadership.
priorKnowledge: Learners studied the main types of district leaders in the preceding period.
materials: P4 SST school reference notes on district leadership
references: P4 Social Studies Notes for Terms 1–3

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the preceding lesson on district leadership and asks "What title is given to the political head of a village?". They use the pupils' answers to connect earlier material to types of district leaders — part b.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall the previous Social Studies period, answer the opening question and identify leaders within their local council.

steps.stage: Development: Remember the types of district leaders
steps.content: Political leaders are elected by citizens. Civic leaders gain office by appointment. Political leaders include mayors and councillors. Civic leaders include district education officers. The CAO heads all district civil servants. Voluntary leaders provide service in organisations. Religious leaders guide communities in religion. Traditional leaders belong to cultural institutions.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the sourced facts under "Remember the types of district leaders", including "Political leaders are elected by citizens. Civic leaders gain office by appointment." They explain the roles and ask "What title is given to the head of the municipality?" to check learners' understanding.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read and copy the points, compare examples of district leadership and answer the teacher's questions about duties and positions.

steps.content: What title is given to the political head of a village? | What title is given to the head of the municipality? | Who is the president’s representative in the district? | How is a Veterinary officer different from an Agricultural officer?
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher gives the original sourced questions, beginning with "What title is given to the political head of a village?" and "What title is given to the head of the municipality?". They supervise learners' written responses and check their answers against the leadership notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the sourced exercise independently, consult the facts in their notes and correct inaccurate answers after marking.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher evaluates learning using "Who is the president’s representative in the district?" and "How is a Veterinary officer different from an Agricultural officer?". They recap the source-grounded points and assign the remaining revision question for later practice.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners give oral answers, state one important district-leadership duty and correct their work in their books.

assessment: Check written and oral responses to "What title is given to the political head of a village?", "What title is given to the head of the municipality?", and "Who is the president’s representative in the district?" and mark against the source material.
homework: Complete the sourced question "How is a Veterinary officer different from an Agricultural officer?" in the Social Studies book.
